chunks: And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from al-‘Amraki, from Ṣandal, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for the one who performs the Ziyārah of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) every month?' He replied to him, 'The reward of one hundred thousand martyrs, like the martyrs of Badr.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husain every month?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) promising the reward of 100,000 martyrs of Badr for monthly visits to Imam al-Ḥusain (a.s.), highlighting the immense spiritual merit of consistent devotion. This comparison to Badr, the first major battle in Islam, underscores the significance of Ziyārah as a form of spiritual jihad and remembrance of the Ahl al-Bayt's sacrifice. The tradition emphasizes that regular visitation cultivates a deep, ongoing connection to the legacy of martyrdom and divine favor.
